official.status_note: The Fund's page states the call 'Opens on Jan 1, 2027 at 12:00 PM', with final application deadline 15 April 2027 at 12:00 PM and results announced 31 May 2027.
official.tuition_coverage_note: Per the Fund's FAQ, the scholarship does not cover tuition fees directly: host institutions receive 2,000 EUR per semester per scholar, which for master's studies covers tuition or administrative costs, while excess fees remain the scholar's responsibility; for post-master's scholarships the lump sum covers institutional hosting expenses.
benefits: 3,500 EUR per semester paid to each scholar's bank account, at the scholar's full disposal
2,000 EUR per semester per scholar paid to the host institution
Support for a study/research period of 1-2 semesters
Scholarship confirmation issued by the Fund, usable as an enclosure to a visa application
eligibility: Citizenship of a Visegrad country (Czechia, Hungary, Poland, Slovakia) or a Western Balkans / Eastern Partnership country: Albania, Armenia, Azerbaijan, Belarus, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Georgia, Kosovo, Moldova, Montenegro, North Macedonia, Serbia, Ukraine
The country of the applicant's citizenship must be different from the country of the host institution
Applicants must hold a bachelor's or master's degree; the FAQs state that for master's/post-master's scholarships 6+ completed semesters or a bachelor's degree are required
Previous levels of university studies must have been completed in a country other than the host country
The distance between the applicant's current employer/university or permanent residence and the host university/institute should exceed 150 km
Full-time master's level studies or full-time post-master's studies/research for 1-2 semesters

Scanned valid national ID or passport

Only one application per deadline, to one host institution, for one study program or research project

2,000 EUR per semester paid to the host institution, covering tuition or administrative costs for master's studies and institutional hosting expenses for post-master's scholarships

Secure admission or at least a preliminary acceptance at a host institution in Central and Eastern Europe

official.application_route: Online via the Fund's My Visegrad portal; the system opens approximately 45 days before the deadline.
official.citizenship_residency: Open to citizens of Czechia, Hungary, Poland, Slovakia and of Albania, Armenia, Azerbaijan, Belarus, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Georgia, Kosovo, Moldova, Montenegro, North Macedonia, Serbia and Ukraine; the applicant's citizenship country must differ from the host institution's country.
official.international_eligibility: Yes - open to citizens of the Visegrad countries as well as Western Balkans and Eastern Partnership countries; no other nationalities are listed as eligible.
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: All disciplines are supported; the application form offers a choice of 25 disciplines covering the large majority of study fields.
official.research_requirement: Post-master's applicants must submit a letter of acceptance with a detailed (approved) working plan from the host institution.
official.duration: 1-2 semesters of full-time study/research; funding is paid per semester (5-month period)
official.description: The International Visegrad Fund's Visegrad Scholarship Program supports master's and post-master's students and researchers, in all disciplines and any language, for up to two semesters at more than 190 accredited higher-education institutions across Central and Eastern Europe.
official.region: Central and Eastern Europe (V4, Western Balkans and Eastern Partnership countries)
official.program_type: Individual mobility scholarship programme (Master's and post-Master's)
official.english_requirement: No language certificates are required and study/research may be in the host university's native language; the application form itself must be filled out in English.

applicant_utility.summary: The Fund pays 3,500 EUR per semester directly into your account, plus 2,000 EUR per semester to your host institution, so a two-semester stay means 7,000 EUR for you - but travel, accommodation, insurance, visa fees and any tuition above the host's 2,000 EUR are on you. The 2027 round opens on 1 January 2027 and shuts strictly at noon on 15 April 2027, with results by 31 May and funding that cannot start before the September/October 2027 semester. The real filter is the mobility rules: no host in your citizenship country, no return to the country or university of your previous degree, and the host must sit more than 150 km from your current university or permanent residence.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Master's or post-master's students and researchers from V4, Western Balkans or Eastern Partnership countries who can line up a CEE host institution far enough from home to satisfy the 150 km rule.
application_readiness_checklist: Contact host institutions early to obtain at least a preliminary acceptance letter, since admission is your responsibility
Request transcripts covering your last two completed semesters well before April
Arrange sworn or university translations into English for any non-English documents
Confirm in writing with the host university what tuition the 2,000 EUR institutional lump sum will actually cover
Check passport validity and research visa requirements so you can move once results land at the end of May
common_rejection_risks: Choosing a host in your own country of citizenship or in the country where you completed your previous degree
Host institution within 150 km of your current university or permanent residence
Submitting after the noon deadline - the Fund accepts no late applications
Filing more than one application, or several hosts or projects, in a single round
Uploading documents that are neither in English nor accompanied by a certified translation
Failing to disclose a concurrent scholarship such as Erasmus, which the Fund may treat as grounds to withdraw its offer
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Travel to and from the host country, accommodation and daily living costs beyond the 3,500 EUR per semester, health insurance, visa/residence permit fees, and any tuition or administrative charges above the 2,000 EUR per semester the host institution receives.
document_audit: Everything is uploaded to My Visegrad - no documents are sent by post - and PDF is the recommended format
If admission tests or interviews fall after the deadline, proof of application or preliminary acceptance is accepted, but the final acceptance letter must be on file before you sign the contract
A second-semester installment requires transcripts showing 30+ ECTS credits plus host enrolment confirmation, or supervisor-signed progress reports at post-master's level
Money is only released after the host university confirms your arrival in writing on letterhead with signature and stamp
alerts: The application system only goes live about 45 days before the deadline, so prepare documents before the January opening
Because results publish at the end of May, funding cannot start before the fall semester (September/October at the earliest)
It is an attendance scholarship - you must remain at the host institution for the entire period
Recipients must acknowledge the Fund in scholarly documentation and public events and use its logo
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Register on My Visegrad, upload the complete document set before 15 April 2027 12:00 PM, respond to any eligibility checks, then receive results by email and the Fund's website by 31 May 2027, sign the posted contract, and get the first payment released after the host confirms arrival.
